subject: CAIQ & network assertion pack request — BluePine audit
messages:
From: Lisa Wong <lisa.wong@bluepine.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: BluePine Security Team <security@bluepine.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: CAIQ / network assertion pack for Dedicated / Private deployments

Hi Connor,

We're starting the security review for the integration between BluePine and Redwood. Our SOC 2 and SIG reviewers requested a focused CAIQ-style "network assertion pack" for the Dedicated/Private deployment options (we're evaluating both). Specifically they asked for:

- A single-page logical network diagram showing control-plane vs data-plane separation for Dedicated and Private (per-region variant if applicable)
- A short narrative (~1 page) that ties network segmentation to CAIQ control mappings (e.g., SC- network controls, boundary claims)
- Evidence pointers: firewall rule screenshots or export, KMS boundary description, tenancy isolation proof, and any per-VPC routing constraints
- A delta/notes file listing anything that differs between Redwood Hosted and Dedicated/Private in scope for the CAIQ questions

Can you confirm whether you can produce these artifacts by the end of next week? Also: do you have a preferred format for the control mapping (CSV, spreadsheet, or table in PDF)?

Thanks — Lisa
Lisa Wong
Security Program Manager, BluePine
lisa.wong@bluepine.ai

---

Hi Lisa — thanks for the clear ask. We can assemble the requested pack. Proposed plan: 

1) Deliverables:
   - Network assertion diagram (PNG) showing both Dedicated and Private flows with control/data-plane separation and egress gates
   - CAIQ mapping PDF (one-page narrative + table)
   - Control delta CSV (columns: control_id, hosted_behavior, dedicated_behavior, notes)
   - Evidence stubs (firewall rule export, KMS boundary statement)

2) Format: we typically provide the control mapping as a CSV and a PDF narrative for auditors. The CSV is easiest for your reviewers to ingest.

3) Timeline: initial draft by Monday 2026-11-16 COB, final pack by Wednesday 2026-11-18 if no major clarifications.

Looping in Kimberly and Karthik to own diagram and control mapping review. Kimberly — can you produce the diagram + narrative? Karthik — will you prepare the control delta and grab the firewall export + KMS blurb?

Connor

Connor — I can take the diagram and the one-page narrative. Notes on scope: 

- Diagram will show three zones: control-plane (management/control services), tenant-data-plane (inference traffic), and shared-infra (logging/metrics/ops). I will annotate KMS boundaries and the default egress choke points we expose in Dedicated and Private.
- For Private (VPC-on-customer-side) I will include the recommended peering/CCM patterns and call out the optional airgap deployments (on-prem) with brief notes about operator-managed routing.
- I will generate the diagram as a high-res PNG and include an editable SVG/Visio export for your auditors.

Attachments I will prepare: redwood-network-assertion-diagram-20261115.png (PNG), redwood-network-assertion-diagram-20261115.svg (source).

Hi Lisa — attached is the initial assertion pack for your reviewers. Contents included in the zip (files listed below as separate attachments for quick reference):

- redwood-network-assertion-diagram-20261115.png (single-page logical diagram; PNG)
- redwood-caIQ-summary-20261115.pdf (one-page narrative + CAIQ mapping table)
- control-matrix-delta-20261115.csv (control_id, hosted_behavior, dedicated_behavior, notes)
- firewall_rules_export_20261114.txt (export of effective firewall rules for Dedicated pools)
- kms-boundary-statement-20261114.txt (short blurb from infra on KMS key scoping)

Drive link (auditor view): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cCcAIQpack
HubSpot ticket: HS-2345 (BluePine SOC2 intake)

Short notes / clarifications:
- The biggest delta buyers usually ask about is egress handling: Dedicated includes an explicit customer-configurable egress list and per-tenant NAT; Private (VPC) depends on your network policies but we document recommended choke points. See control-matrix-delta-20261115.csv row SC-6.
- KMS: customer-managed key option is available for Private; for Dedicated we use tenant-scoped keys in the customer-managed KMS when requested — see kms-boundary-statement.
- We did not include low-level firewall screenshots but included an export and a mapping referencing rule ids; if the auditors need packet-capture level evidence, let us know and we can pull a sanitized sample under NDA.

If you want a short walkthrough with the security reviewers I can schedule a 30-minute call this week — propose Wed 2026-11-18 10:00 AM PT.

Thanks,
Connor
